newsitem.title: MEXICO: Bear Stearns revises EPS on Mexico cement firms.
newsitem.headline: Bear Stearns revises EPS on Mexico cement firms.

text.p: Bear Stearns has revised its earnings estimates for three Mexican cement companies, Cemex, Apasco and Grupo Cementos Chihuahua, to reflect the prospects for firm economic growth and a stable peso, the brokerage said Thursday.

A report from analysts Sobani Warner and Daniel Altman raised Cemex's projected 1996 earnings per American depositary receipt to $1.64 from $1.59. Earnings estimated for 1997, however, were lowered to $0.65 per ADR, from $0.83.

"Contrary to economic reality, bottom line earnings for Cemex for 1997 decline as our outlook for inflation improves. Monetary gains decline with the expectation of a significant lowering of inflation in 1997," Warner and Altman said.
Bear Stearns maintained its "neutral" rating on the company.
The report upped Apasco's estimated earnings per ADR for 1996 and 1997 to $2.48 and $2.67, respectively, from $2.08 and $2.00.

"It is the expectation of higher cement prices and lower inflationary pressures on production costs that have led us to increase our estimates and raise our price target," the report said about Apasco.
Apasco's target ADR price is now $42 for 1997, but Bear Stearns maintained its neutral rating for the stock.

"Our forecast for (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization) is $225 million for 1996 and $257 million for 1997. These figures are roughly 15 percent higher than for our previous estimates," the report added.
The report meanwhile upped earnings per share estimates for Grupo Cementos Chihuahua to $0.07 and $0.08 for 1996 and 1997, respectively, from $0.06 and $0.07.

"We maintain our Attractive rating on the shares as company fundamentals are still solid -- demand in Mexico is improving and the market in the southwestern region is still strong," the report said. Warner and Altman said they would only recommend buying on weakness for GCC given its 60 percent appreciation since February.
